subject: ra-aid
title: Tool loop eval()s model output with default builtins, so the shell approval gate is fully bypassable
evidence: ra_aid/agent_backends/ciayn_agent.py:345 (globals_dict = tool funcs only, __builtins__ not suppressed), :533,691 (eval of model text), :45-90 (validation accepts any single ast.Call, e.g. __import__('os').system(...))
one_why: RA.Aid proves the inverse lesson: per-command approval (shell.py:89-109, well-tested) is worthless when the executor itself runs untrusted expressions with full Python builtins; any code-as-actions design needs AST allow-list + __builtins__:{} or a real sandbox before the approval story means anything

subject: ra-aid
title: Class docstring advertises 'Sandboxed code execution environment' -- no sandbox exists anywhere in the tree
evidence: ra_aid/agent_backends/ciayn_agent.py:122 vs grep -i sandbox|bwrap|seatbelt|landlock ra_aid --include='*.py': only that docstring line hits
one_why: Reviewers score honesty about what enforcement does not exist; this is the anti-pattern with teeth -- the claim actively misleads readers of the code, not just README users

subject: ra-aid
title: CIAYN backend: tool calls are model-written Python expressions validated by ast.parse, with LLM-based tool-call extraction as per-model rescue
evidence: ra_aid/agent_backends/ciayn_agent.py:100-133 (CIAYN doc), :45-90 (AST validation), :483-500 (models_params-gated attempt_llm_tool_extraction re-parses malformed calls with a second LLM), bundleable multi-call execution :507-563
one_why: The shape (free-form Python as the tool protocol, per-model quirk table deciding when to salvage a bad call with an LLM) is a real alternative to JSON tool-calling that survives contact with weak open models -- port the protocol idea, none of the exec machinery

subject: ra-aid
title: Repeat breaker is a single-fingerprint memory (last call only) over a hardcoded tool list, duplicated ~120 LOC across bundled and single paths
evidence: ra_aid/agent_backends/ciayn_agent.py:137-150 (NO_REPEAT_TOOLS), :505-528 vs :583-660 (copy-pasted fingerprint blocks), :531-537 (AST parse failure silently skips the check)
one_why: Weakest variant found in corpus: two alternating calls defeat it, and the fail-open on unparseable params means the breaker disappears exactly when the model gets weird -- a cautionary floor under the loop-detection ladder

subject: ra-aid
title: Context overflow handled by pure head-drop with a bytes/2 estimator -- no summarization tier, silent history loss
one_why: Contrast with pi's projected-context trigger: RA.Aid's in-loop estimate can be off 2-4x vs the real tokenizer, so overflow lands as raw message loss; only saving grace is DB-backed key-facts memory surviving the drops

subject: ra-aid
title: Dedicated GC agents garbage-collect accumulated research notes, key facts, and key snippets
evidence: ra_aid/agents/research_notes_gc_agent.py (386 LOC), ra_aid/agents/key_facts_gc_agent.py, ra_aid/agents/key_snippets_gc_agent.py; store side at ra_aid/tools/memory.py:230-395
one_why: Nobody else in the corpus treats the long-term note store as needing its own janitor agent -- the complement to memory-files that keeps the store from becoming the new context bloat

subject: ra-aid
title: Tool-call failure fallback chain seeded from a frozen 2025-02 snapshot of the Berkeley gorilla function-calling leaderboard
evidence: ra_aid/tool_leaderboard.py:1-5 ('Data extracted at 2/10/2025'), ra_aid/fallback_handler.py:18,42-49 (supported_top_tool_models + experimental_fallback_handler gate)
one_why: Auto-picking fallback tool-calling models from an external quality ranking is a genuinely new idea here; the frozen-snapshot staleness is the flaw to fix if the idea is ever ported

subject: ra-aid
title: Server binds 0.0.0.0 by default with an unauthenticated /v1/spawn_agent; cowboy+server merely prints a warning
one_why: Same deferral shape as openharness-4 but worse default: on a LAN laptop this is an open RPC to run an autonomous coding agent (and, via ra-aid-1, arbitrary code)

subject: ra-aid
title: SWE-bench dataset generator in-repo but no CI workflow references any eval
one_why: Same convergence bucket as openharness-10: eval tooling exists for users, never gates the repo, so the verification ceiling stays 6
